I'm afraid if we use our secondary color for links, that users will no longer recognize this as an active link.

Links tend to stay the same color in an application (albeit we do change their colors on the browser chrome ecosystem when you have a theme installed so it mixes well with the theme), so they can be recognized as a link.

If we use gray here I'm afraid people may either think it's disabled or won't see this a link. I'd recommend just keeping all links the actual link colors, for usability and accessibility purposes, and perhaps trying to play with hierarchy if you want those two to be less important than the Learn more.

By the way - our yellow warning color is currently not accessible against white. If we use the hollow version of our icons, that makes it even harder to see them against the background. I figure accessibility is going to point this out.

We're actively working on improving our color palette, so we could provide you a better yellow in the future, but for now I wanted to flag that this will most likely be flagged by accessibility.

The resolution I recommend here in the short term is to keep the yellow we have in the codebase today until the systems team finishes tidying up our color palette. Then we can file a bug to replace our yellow warning color in the codebase once our new palette is in.
